meta.title: Entry Check: Advanced Grammar and Voice

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?
choices: The committee approved the proposal after a long meeting.
The proposal was approved after a long meeting.
After a long meeting, the committee approved the proposal.
The committee will approve the proposal after a long meeting.
questions.explanation: The passive voice puts the subject in the subject position and uses a form of be with the past participle approved.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Choose the present-tense verb that agrees with the singular subject: The author of the essays ___ revising each chapter now.
choices: is
are
am
be
questions.explanation: The singular subject author takes the present-tense verb is, even though the prepositional phrase of the essays comes between them.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses subject-verb inversion after a fronted negative phrase?
choices: Only after the bell did the guests leave.
Only after the bell the guests did leave.
Only after the bell left the guests did.
Only after the bell did the guests left.
questions.explanation: Only after the bell is a fronted negative phrase, so did the guests leave correctly inverts the subject and verb.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: By the time the teacher noticed the folder was missing, another pupil ___ it.
choices: has taken
takes
had taken
is taking
questions.explanation: Had taken is in the past perfect because the pupil took the folder before the teacher noticed that it was missing.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that uses the interrogative mood.
choices: Where will the team practice after the tournament?
The team will practice after the tournament.
Although the team will practice after the tournament, the coaches will watch.
The coaches will watch the team practice after the tournament.
questions.explanation: The sentence asks where the team will practice, so it uses the interrogative mood.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Sentence Mood

questions.prompt: After the collision, Carlos hurt ___.
choices: himself
themselves
herself
itself
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun agrees with the singular antecedent Carlos, so himself is correct.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a modal to express certainty based on the available evidence?
choices: The measurements match exactly, so the device must be working.
The measurements match exactly, so the device might be working.
The measurements match exactly, so the device may be working.
The measurements match exactly, so the device can be working.
questions.explanation: Must expresses the certainty inferred from the speaker's conclusion.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes an unreal condition and result in the past?
choices: If Leah left earlier, she will catch the train.
If Leah had left earlier, she would have caught the train.
If Leah had left earlier, she would catch the train.
If Leah would leave earlier, she would have caught the train.
questions.explanation: The correct option uses the third conditional: had left sets an unreal past condition, and would have caught states its unreal result.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a sentence fragment?
choices: Because the roads were flooded, the buses were delayed all morning.
While the roads were flooded, the buses were delayed all morning.
Because the roads were flooded and the buses were delayed all morning.
After the roads were flooded, the buses were delayed and the drivers waited.
questions.explanation: The correct option is a sentence fragment because the dependent clause introduced by because has no main clause.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: By the time the judges arrive, the technicians ___ the winner's trophy.
choices: will have polished
will polish
had polished
have polished
questions.explanation: The future perfect will have polished indicates that the polishing will be complete before the judges arrive.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Choose the verb that agrees with the singular subject: On the bulletin board, a list of approved names ___.
choices: appears
appear
appearing
appeared
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun phrase a list of approved names, so appears is the correct present-tense verb.
questions.skill: Agreement with a Singular Noun Phrase
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Subject-Verb Agreement

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a comma splice?
choices: The band began playing and the audience began clapping.
The band began playing; the audience began clapping.
The band began playing when the audience began clapping.
The band began playing, the audience began clapping.
questions.explanation: The correct option is a comma splice because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence reports the statement I am ready to begin using the standard shift to reported speech?
choices: She said that she was ready to begin.
She said that she is ready to begin.
She said that she has been ready to begin.
She said that she had been ready to begin.
questions.explanation: The simple present in the direct statement normally shifts to the simple past in reported speech, producing she was ready to begin.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Reported Speech

questions.prompt: Select the sentence in which the participial phrase tasting the soup logically modifies the chef.
choices: Tasting the soup, the table was set for dinner.
The chef, tasting the soup, decided that it needed salt.
After tasting the soup, the waiter carried the empty bowl away.
Tasting the soup, it was the chef who decided that it needed salt.
questions.explanation: In the selected sentence, tasting the soup describes the chef, who is the subject of the main clause.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Participial Modifiers

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the preposition correctly?
choices: Despite of the rain, the soccer match continued.
Despite from the rain, the soccer match continued.
Despite to the rain, the soccer match continued.
Despite the rain, the soccer match continued.
questions.explanation: Despite is followed directly by the noun phrase the rain, so no second preposition belongs after it.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Choose the relative pronoun that correctly completes the sentence: The student ___ essay won the contest was recognized at the assembly.
choices: whose
who
which
where
questions.explanation: Whose expresses possession and identifies the essay that belongs to the student.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause.
choices: After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance, the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance; the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance, and the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
questions.explanation: The introductory clause After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance is followed by a comma before the independent clause.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Clauses and Comma Usage

questions.prompt: Which sentence avoids a dangling modifier?
choices: Walking into the room, the trophy was placed on the table.
Walking into the room, she placed the trophy on the table.
The trophy was placed on the table while walking into the room.
While walking into the room, the trophy was placed on the table.
questions.explanation: In the correct sentence, she is the subject of the main clause, so the introductory phrase Walking into the room logically modifies her.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the infinitive correctly after the verb require?
choices: The rules require every participant to check in before the final round.
The rules require every participant to checks in before the final round.
The rules require every participant to checked in before the final round.
The rules require every participant to checking in before the final round.
questions.explanation: The infinitive to is followed by the base verb check in, not an inflected or -ing form.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which conjunction correctly introduces the contrast in this sentence? ___ the deadline had passed, Maya asked whether the office could still accept her application.
choices: Even though
As
Provided that
Before
questions.explanation: Even though introduces a contrast between the deadline having passed and Maya's request that the office might still accept her application.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the imperative mood?
choices: Close the door when you leave.
Closes the door when you leave.
Closed the door when you leave.
Closing the door when you leave.
questions.explanation: The imperative mood gives a direct command, so the sentence begins with the base-form verb Close without a subject.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
choices: The library closes at six p.m.; students must return books before then.
The library closes at six p.m., students must return books before then.
The library closes at six p.m.; and students must return books before then.
The library closes at six p.m. students must return books before then.
questions.explanation: A semicolon can join two complete independent clauses, and the clause after it should not begin with the conjunction and.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Select the sentence in which used to expresses a past habit rather than a state of being accustomed.
choices: Amara used to work later than usual when she lived abroad.
Amara is used to work later than usual when she lived abroad.
Amara used to working later than usual when she lived abroad.
Amara is used to working later than usual now.
questions.explanation: Used to followed by the base verb work describes Amara's past habit.
questions.skill: Distinguishing used to from be used to
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Tricky Verb Usage

questions.prompt: Choose the object pronoun that correctly fills the blank: After the judges selected the winners, the reporters asked ___ for comments.
choices: them
they
their
theirs
questions.explanation: Them is the object pronoun for the reporters, who are the people doing the asking.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a restrictive clause without implying that every student volunteers at the library?
choices: Students who volunteer at the library will receive a thank-you gift.
Students, who volunteer at the library, will receive a thank-you gift.
Students who volunteer at the library, will receive a thank-you gift.
Students, who volunteer at the library will receive a thank-you gift.
questions.explanation: Because the clause identifies which students qualify, it is restrictive and should not be set off by commas.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence expresses its action in the active voice?
choices: The engineers redesigned the ventilation system.
The ventilation system was redesigned by the engineers.
The ventilation system had been redesigned by the engineers.
The ventilation system is being redesigned by the engineers.
questions.explanation: The engineers are the subject performing the action, so the sentence uses the active voice.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Voice

questions.prompt: Choose the verb that correctly agrees with the singular subject and fits the present-tense sentence: The committee ___ the work among four teams every week.
choices: divides
divide
dividing
divided
questions.explanation: The singular subject committee takes the present-tense verb divides.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly forms an embedded question?
choices: The coach asked the players where they should meet.
The coach asked the players where should they meet.
The coach asked the players where did they meet.
The coach asked the players where they did meet.
questions.explanation: An embedded question after asked uses statement-like word order, with the subject they before the auxiliary should.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: In which sentence do both adjectives directly modify the noun kitten?
choices: The small kitten gray slept.
The kitten small gray slept.
The small gray kitten slept.
The gray the small kitten slept.
questions.explanation: In The small gray kitten slept, both small and gray directly modify the noun kitten, and the article comes first.
questions.skill: Placing multiple adjectives before a noun
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: According to the sentence, how many independent clauses does it contain? After the game ended, the players left the field, and the announcer summarized the match.
choices: one
two
three
four
questions.explanation: The clauses about the players leaving and the announcer summarizing are independent, while the introductory clause beginning with after is dependent.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence as an adjective after the linking verb: The soup tasted ___.
choices: salty
saltiness
salt
saltily
questions.explanation: Salty is an adjective that functions as a predicate adjective after the linking verb tasted.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the conditional mood?
choices: If the deadline extends, we can submit the form later.
The deadline extends, so we can submit the form later.
How can we submit the form after the deadline?
Submit the form after the deadline.
questions.explanation: The if-clause states a condition and the main clause gives its consequence, which makes the sentence conditional.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Looking forward to ___ you again.
choices: hear
hearing
heard
hears
questions.explanation: Hearing is a gerund, which is required after the preposition to in the phrase looking forward to.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct present-tense verb: The captain and the two guards ___ in the gym now.
choices: has
have
had
is
questions.explanation: The compound subject the captain and the two guards is plural, so it takes have in the present tense.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Subject-Verb Agreement

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon to introduce a complete clause?
choices: The rule is simple: arrive by eight.
The rule is simple: to arrive by eight.
The rule is simple: arriving by eight.
The rule is simple: arrived by eight.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the complete imperative clause arrive by eight.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: The students completed the assignment, and ___ turned it in on time.
choices: it
they
them
their
questions.explanation: The plural antecedent students requires the plural subject pronoun they in the second independent clause.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an em dash to separate two complete sentences?
choices: The experiment failed—the sample had been contaminated.
The experiment failed – the sample had been contaminated.
The experiment failed; the sample had been contaminated—.
The experiment failed—the sample had been contaminated, the results were unreliable.
questions.explanation: The em dash separates two complete sentences while adding information that explains why the experiment failed.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence presents three actions in parallel structure?
choices: The volunteers sorted, packed, and labeled the donated books.
The volunteers sorted, packed, and were labeling the donated books.
The volunteers sorted, to pack, and labeled the donated books.
The volunteers sorting, packed, and labeled the donated books.
questions.explanation: The correct option uses three simple past-tense verbs in the same grammatical form: sorted, packed, and labeled.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the simple past tense consistently for both main verbs?
choices: Yesterday, the guide answers questions and pointed out several details.
Yesterday, the guide answered questions and points out several details.
Yesterday, the guide answered questions and will point out several details.
Yesterday, the guide answered questions and pointed out several details.
questions.explanation: The correct option uses the simple past tense for both coordinated verbs, answered and pointed, consistently with the time marker yesterday.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which determiner correctly completes the sentence? ___ students attended the workshop than had registered.
choices: Fewer
Less
Little
Much
questions.explanation: Fewer is the correct determiner for the countable plural noun students.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the possessive apostrophe correctly?
choices: The scientists report was cited by the review panel.
The scientist's report was cited by the review panel.
The scientist report's was cited by the review panel.
The scientist's were cited by the review panel.
questions.explanation: The correct option places the apostrophe in scientist's to show that the report belongs to one scientist.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Of the two bicycles, the red one is ___ than the blue one.
choices: faster
fastest
more fast
most fast
questions.explanation: Because the sentence compares exactly two bicycles, faster is the correct comparative form.
questions.skill: Forming a Comparative with Two Items
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Comparative Adjectives

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood?
choices: The director insisted that the report be finished by Friday.
The director insisted that the report was finished by Friday.
The director insisted that the report is finished by Friday.
The director insisted that the report has finished by Friday.
questions.explanation: After an expression of insistence, the subjunctive uses the base form be rather than a conjugated form of be.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an exclamatory sentence?
choices: How brilliantly the young pianist performed!
The young pianist performed brilliantly at the recital.
Did the young pianist perform brilliantly at the recital?
Perform brilliantly at the recital tonight.
questions.explanation: The how construction and exclamation mark express strong admiration rather than merely asking for information.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses hyphens correctly in a compound modifier?
choices: The state-of-the-art design won an award.
The state-of-the art design won an award.
The state of the art design won an award.
The state-of-the-art-design won an award.
questions.explanation: State-of-the-art is a fully hyphenated compound modifier placed before the noun design.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly uses the past progressive to describe an action in progress at a specific past time.
choices: At eight o'clock, the students were reviewing the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
At eight o'clock, the students reviewed the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
At eight o'clock, the students are reviewing the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
At eight o'clock, the students was reviewing the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
questions.explanation: The past progressive was reviewing describes the students' action in progress at the stated past time.
questions.skill: Using the past progressive for actions in progress
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Verb Tense and Aspect

questions.prompt: Which conjunction correctly expresses the direct reason in this sentence? ___ the evidence was incomplete, the researchers repeated the experiment.
choices: Because
Although
Unless
Until
questions.explanation: Because introduces the incomplete evidence as the direct reason the researchers repeated the experiment.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which noun phrase follows the conventional English order of size, age, color, and material?
choices: a small old brown leather suitcase
an old small brown leather suitcase
a leather old brown small suitcase
a brown old small leather suitcase
questions.explanation: The first option follows the conventional sequence of size, age, color, and material before the noun.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: The tutor recommended the exercise to Priya and ___.
choices: me
I
myself
mine
questions.explanation: Me is an object pronoun because it follows the preposition to and identifies who received the recommendation.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a correctly punctuated appositive?
choices: My neighbor, a retired engineer, restored the antique clock.
My neighbor a retired engineer, restored the antique clock.
My neighbor, a retired engineer restored the antique clock.
My neighbor a retired engineer restored, the antique clock.
questions.explanation: The noun phrase a retired engineer identifies My neighbor and is correctly enclosed by a pair of commas.
questions.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Choose the present-tense verb that agrees with the singular subject: The author of the essays ___ revising each chapter now.
choices: is
are
am
be
kept.explanation: The singular subject author takes the present-tense verb is, even though the prepositional phrase of the essays comes between them.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Choose the relative pronoun that correctly completes the sentence: The student ___ essay won the contest was recognized at the assembly.
choices: whose
who
which
where
kept.explanation: Whose expresses possession and identifies the essay that belongs to the student.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which conjunction correctly introduces the contrast in this sentence? ___ the deadline had passed, Maya asked whether the office could still accept her application.
choices: Even though
As
Provided that
Before
kept.explanation: Even though introduces a contrast between the deadline having passed and Maya's request that the office might still accept her application.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which sentence uses the imperative mood?
choices: Close the door when you leave.
Closes the door when you leave.
Closed the door when you leave.
Closing the door when you leave.
kept.explanation: The imperative mood gives a direct command, so the sentence begins with the base-form verb Close without a subject.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Choose the object pronoun that correctly fills the blank: After the judges selected the winners, the reporters asked ___ for comments.
choices: them
they
their
theirs
kept.explanation: Them is the object pronoun for the reporters, who are the people doing the asking.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence as an adjective after the linking verb: The soup tasted ___.
choices: salty
saltiness
salt
saltily
kept.explanation: Salty is an adjective that functions as a predicate adjective after the linking verb tasted.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which determiner correctly completes the sentence? ___ students attended the workshop than had registered.
choices: Fewer
Less
Little
Much
kept.explanation: Fewer is the correct determiner for the countable plural noun students.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: After the collision, Carlos hurt ___.
choices: himself
themselves
herself
itself
kept.explanation: The reflexive pronoun agrees with the singular antecedent Carlos, so himself is correct.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon to introduce a complete clause?
choices: The rule is simple: arrive by eight.
The rule is simple: to arrive by eight.
The rule is simple: arriving by eight.
The rule is simple: arrived by eight.
kept.explanation: The colon introduces the complete imperative clause arrive by eight.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which sentence uses a modal to express certainty based on the available evidence?
choices: The measurements match exactly, so the device must be working.
The measurements match exactly, so the device might be working.
The measurements match exactly, so the device may be working.
The measurements match exactly, so the device can be working.
kept.explanation: Must expresses the certainty inferred from the speaker's conclusion.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which noun phrase follows the conventional English order of size, age, color, and material?
choices: a small old brown leather suitcase
an old small brown leather suitcase
a leather old brown small suitcase
a brown old small leather suitcase
kept.explanation: The first option follows the conventional sequence of size, age, color, and material before the noun.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: By the time the judges arrive, the technicians ___ the winner's trophy.
choices: will have polished
will polish
had polished
have polished
kept.explanation: The future perfect will have polished indicates that the polishing will be complete before the judges arrive.
kept.topic: Tester 1 of 9: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct present-tense verb: The captain and the two guards ___ in the gym now.
choices: has
have
had
is
kept.explanation: The compound subject the captain and the two guards is plural, so it takes have in the present tense.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Subject-Verb Agreement

kept.prompt: Identify the sentence that correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause.
choices: After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance, the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance; the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance, and the maintenance crew cleared the fallen branches.
kept.explanation: The introductory clause After the storm had damaged the eastern entrance is followed by a comma before the independent clause.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Clauses and Comma Usage

kept.prompt: Select the sentence in which the participial phrase tasting the soup logically modifies the chef.
choices: Tasting the soup, the table was set for dinner.
The chef, tasting the soup, decided that it needed salt.
After tasting the soup, the waiter carried the empty bowl away.
Tasting the soup, it was the chef who decided that it needed salt.
kept.explanation: In the selected sentence, tasting the soup describes the chef, who is the subject of the main clause.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Participial Modifiers

kept.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly uses the past progressive to describe an action in progress at a specific past time.
choices: At eight o'clock, the students were reviewing the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
At eight o'clock, the students reviewed the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
At eight o'clock, the students are reviewing the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
At eight o'clock, the students was reviewing the lesson when the fire alarm sounded.
kept.explanation: The past progressive was reviewing describes the students' action in progress at the stated past time.
kept.skill: Using the past progressive for actions in progress
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Verb Tense and Aspect

kept.prompt: Identify the sentence that uses the interrogative mood.
choices: Where will the team practice after the tournament?
The team will practice after the tournament.
Although the team will practice after the tournament, the coaches will watch.
The coaches will watch the team practice after the tournament.
kept.explanation: The sentence asks where the team will practice, so it uses the interrogative mood.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Sentence Mood

kept.prompt: Select the sentence in which used to expresses a past habit rather than a state of being accustomed.
choices: Amara used to work later than usual when she lived abroad.
Amara is used to work later than usual when she lived abroad.
Amara used to working later than usual when she lived abroad.
Amara is used to working later than usual now.
kept.explanation: Used to followed by the base verb work describes Amara's past habit.
kept.skill: Distinguishing used to from be used to
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Tricky Verb Usage

kept.prompt: Which sentence uses hyphens correctly in a compound modifier?
choices: The state-of-the-art design won an award.
The state-of-the art design won an award.
The state of the art design won an award.
The state-of-the-art-design won an award.
kept.explanation: State-of-the-art is a fully hyphenated compound modifier placed before the noun design.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an em dash to separate two complete sentences?
choices: The experiment failed—the sample had been contaminated.
The experiment failed – the sample had been contaminated.
The experiment failed; the sample had been contaminated—.
The experiment failed—the sample had been contaminated, the results were unreliable.
kept.explanation: The em dash separates two complete sentences while adding information that explains why the experiment failed.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which sentence is in the conditional mood?
choices: If the deadline extends, we can submit the form later.
The deadline extends, so we can submit the form later.
How can we submit the form after the deadline?
Submit the form after the deadline.
kept.explanation: The if-clause states a condition and the main clause gives its consequence, which makes the sentence conditional.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: According to the sentence, how many independent clauses does it contain? After the game ended, the players left the field, and the announcer summarized the match.
choices: one
two
three
four
kept.explanation: The clauses about the players leaving and the announcer summarizing are independent, while the introductory clause beginning with after is dependent.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Which sentence is an exclamatory sentence?
choices: How brilliantly the young pianist performed!
The young pianist performed brilliantly at the recital.
Did the young pianist perform brilliantly at the recital?
Perform brilliantly at the recital tonight.
kept.explanation: The how construction and exclamation mark express strong admiration rather than merely asking for information.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9

kept.prompt: Choose the verb that agrees with the singular subject: On the bulletin board, a list of approved names ___.
choices: appears
appear
appearing
appeared
kept.explanation: The subject is the singular noun phrase a list of approved names, so appears is the correct present-tense verb.
kept.skill: Agreement with a Singular Noun Phrase
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Subject-Verb Agreement

kept.prompt: Which sentence reports the statement I am ready to begin using the standard shift to reported speech?
choices: She said that she was ready to begin.
She said that she is ready to begin.
She said that she has been ready to begin.
She said that she had been ready to begin.
kept.explanation: The simple present in the direct statement normally shifts to the simple past in reported speech, producing she was ready to begin.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Reported Speech

kept.prompt: Of the two bicycles, the red one is ___ than the blue one.
choices: faster
fastest
more fast
most fast
kept.explanation: Because the sentence compares exactly two bicycles, faster is the correct comparative form.
kept.skill: Forming a Comparative with Two Items
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Comparative Adjectives

kept.prompt: Which sentence expresses its action in the active voice?
choices: The engineers redesigned the ventilation system.
The ventilation system was redesigned by the engineers.
The ventilation system had been redesigned by the engineers.
The ventilation system is being redesigned by the engineers.
kept.explanation: The engineers are the subject performing the action, so the sentence uses the active voice.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 1 of 9: Voice

rejected.prompt: Each of the students in the class ___ the essay on time last Friday.
choices: have submitted
has submitted
is submitting
were submitting
rejected.explanation: The singular subject Each takes the singular verb phrase has submitted, even though the phrase in the class names many students.

rejected.prompt: Choose the relative pronoun that correctly completes the sentence: The manager called the designer ___ she needed the revised plans.
choices: who
whom
whose
which
rejected.explanation: The pronoun refers to the designer as the object of called, so the objective form whom is required.

rejected.prompt: Ms. Ortiz, ___ teaches biology at our school, will lead the workshop.
choices: who
whom
whose
which
rejected.explanation: Because the relative clause is nonrestrictive and refers to Ms. Ortiz, the subject pronoun who is required.

rejected.prompt: Each volunteer received three ___ for the event.
choices: assignments
assignment
assignment's
assignments'
rejected.explanation: Because three is a plural number word, the count noun assignment takes the plural form assignments.

rejected.prompt: Choose the pronoun that correctly completes the sentence: Although the museum was busy, the guide unlocked the entrance to ___.
choices: it
its
it's
them
rejected.explanation: The pronoun it refers to the museum and correctly serves as the object of the preposition to.

rejected.prompt: Choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence: The puppy carried the toy to its bed and ___ down beside it.
choices: laid
lay
lied
lays
rejected.explanation: The intransitive verb lay correctly describes the puppy reclining after carrying the toy.

rejected.prompt: Choose the conjunction that correctly completes the sentence by expressing a direct result: The battery was nearly empty, ___ the flashlight suddenly went dark.
choices: because
although
so
unless
rejected.explanation: The conjunction so correctly joins two independent clauses and signals that the flashlight went dark as a result of the nearly empty battery.
